title: A nonzero group norm certifies independence of the entire orbit
summary: An exact independence certificate in modular representation theory and a reusable counterexample to importing positive-definite Gram-matrix intuition into finite fields.
content: For any linear action of H=(C3)^r over any characteristic-three field, N_H v is nonzero if and only if all 3^r orbit vectors h v are linearly independent. The proof uses K[H]=K[z_1,...,z_r]/(z_i^3): every nonzero ideal contains product z_i^2=N_H. For the project's particular block action, rank(N_H)=sum over spanning column subsets S of 3^(|S|-r), with minimum 4^(m-r) exactly for coordinate subgroups. A tensor family has orbit dimension 3^k but Hermitian Gram rank one.
whenToUse: An exact independence certificate in modular representation theory and a reusable counterexample to importing positive-definite Gram-matrix intuition into finite fields.
limitations: The independence theorem is general for the stated group/characteristic, while the rank formula is action-specific. Incompressibility inside one orbit does not exclude other dictionaries or implicit evaluation. Enumerating column subsets still costs exponentially in m.
